topic: DNACPR and ceilings of care documentation

audits.title: 259 AN AUDIT OF DNACPR FORM USAGE IN A LEVEL 4 HOSPITAL FOLLOWING RE-DESIGN AND IMPLICATIONS FOR ITS FUTURE USE
audits.setting: Hospital-wide medical and surgical wards, level 4 hospital (ICU excluded)

cycle1.result: 19% of inpatients had forms; 68% DNACPR; 76% of forms had a TEP (vs 56% on old forms).

audits.intervention: Redesigned green DNACPR form with yes/no resuscitation choice and TEP moved to the front page.

cycle2.result: 15.7% (100) had a form, 92% stating DNAR; 99% of those not for CPR had a TEP; doctor's name and grade on all forms.

audits.other_findings: 83.3% of patients had no documented resuscitation status, so the yes/no approach is not being used for all patients.
audits.citation: . 259 AN AUDIT OF DNACPR FORM USAGE IN A LEVEL 4 HOSPITAL FOLLOWING RE-DESIGN AND IMPLICATIONS FOR ITS FUTURE USE. Age Ageing. 2022;51(Suppl 3).

audits.title: 2320 DNAR: all or nothing: impact of education sessions Re-audit
audits.standard: Irish Health Service Executive (HSE) national DNAR guidelines
audits.setting: Sligo University Hospital, Model 3 hospital, adult medical inpatients

cycle1.result: DNAR status documented in medical notes 35%; reasoning 32%; patient discussion 45%; reasons if patient discussion excluded 41%; relatives' discussion 48%; reasons if relatives excluded 18%.

audits.intervention: Two education sessions for NCHDs and consultants.

cycle2.result: DNAR status 35% and reasoning 32% (unchanged); patient discussion 61%; reasons if excluded 66%; relatives' discussion 48% (unchanged); reasons if relatives excluded 25%; ceilings of care documentation increased (ICU three-fold, intubation two-fold) but still under 15%.

audits.other_findings: Ceilings of care documentation remained under 15%; authors propose a Ceilings of Care document.
audits.citation: Ramjohn J, Kelly J, Abdalla A, Hamad A, Carvalho J, Gibbons C, et al.. 2320 DNAR: all or nothing: impact of education sessions Re-audit. Age and Ageing. 2024;53(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afae139.039.

audits.title: DNAR: All or Nothing: Impact of Education Sessions Re-Audit in a Model 3 Hospital
audits.standard: National HSE guidelines on DNAR and ceilings of care documentation
audits.setting: Adult medical inpatients, Sligo University Hospital (Model 3 hospital)

cycle1.result: DNAR status in medical notes 35%; reasoning 32%; patient discussion documented 45%; reasons if excluded 41%; relatives' discussion 48%; reasons if excluded 18%.

audits.intervention: Two education sessions for NCHDs and consultants.

cycle2.result: DNAR status 35% and reasoning 32% (unchanged); patient discussion 61%; reasons if excluded 66%; relatives' discussion 48%; reasons if excluded 25%.

audits.other_findings: Ceilings of care documentation increased (ICU admission three-fold, intubation two-fold) but stayed below 15%; a Ceilings of Care document was proposed.

audits.title: The UHL DNACPR Process in Practice: An Audit of Documentation, Communication and Signatory Compliance
audits.setting: 14 wards and Emergency Department, University Hospital Limerick; medical admissions

cycle1.result: 62/72 (86%) signed by an NCHD, 26/72 (36%) by a consultant, 8/72 (11%) by a nurse; 46/72 (63.8%) signed only by an NCHD, 11 of which had no documented discussion.

audits.intervention: Recommended: training on appropriate DNACPR form use for NCHDs, nurses and consultants.
audits.other_findings: 75/247 (23.1%) medically admitted patients had a DNACPR form; 3 were from previous admissions.
audits.citation: McCartan D, Zulkifli N, Kumar P, Abubakr A, Romaniuk J, McManus J. The UHL DNACPR Process in Practice: An Audit of Documentation, Communication and Signatory Compliance. Age and Ageing. 2025;54(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.156.

audits.title: 243 An Audit of Documentation of Resuscitation Status in a Teaching Hospital
audits.standard: National Consent Policy: resuscitation decisions made with patient or family, by the most senior decision maker, and carefully documented
audits.setting: St Columcille's Hospital, Dublin, teaching hospital inpatients

cycle1.result: 25.5% had a DNACPR order; 100% had a form but none fully completed; 48% not endorsed by the consultant; 74% not discussed with patient or no reason documented; 41% no discussion documented.

audits.other_findings: 92% had DNACPR status documented in nursing notes; results to be used in an education session.
audits.citation: McDonough A, O'Hanlon S. 243 An Audit of Documentation of Resuscitation Status in a Teaching Hospital. Age and Ageing. 2019;48(Supplement_3):iii17-iii65. doi:10.1093/ageing/afz103.147.

audits.title: An Audit of the DNACPR Policy at Malta's Mount Carmel Hospital
audits.standard: Hospital DNACPR policy standards (resuscitation form completion)
audits.setting: Five chronic psychiatric inpatient wards, Mount Carmel Hospital, Malta, compared with Saint Vincent De Paule Residence

cycle1.result: Resuscitation form completion 73.47% at MCH vs 94.90% at SVPR; 9.72% vs 61.29% designated Not for CPR.

audits.intervention: Resuscitation training tailored to inpatient psychiatry including decision-making stations.
audits.other_findings: Comorbidities were significantly greater in the SVPR cohort (3.50 vs 2.47).
audits.citation: Warwicker S, Bellizzi A. An Audit of the DNACPR Policy at Malta's Mount Carmel Hospital. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S180-S180.

audits.title: DNACPR Documentation Audit on Old Age Psychiatry Wards in Aneurin Bevan University Health Board (ABUHB) in South Wales
audits.standard: All-Wales DNACPR policy for adults (2015, revised 2024)
audits.setting: Four old age psychiatry wards, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board, South Wales

cycle1.result: Decision date missing in 2 forms; not signed with date and time in 1; not documented in clinical notes in 10; discussion with patient in 9; discussion with IMCA/attorney or family in 20; appropriate signatures in 17; 7 not countersigned in section 6.

audits.other_findings: Different versions of the DNACPR form were in use. Recommended a unified form and adding DNACPR and treatment escalation status to the ward round proforma.
audits.citation: Romeh A, Mosaico G, Elhusseiny M, Boyle P, Kalam T. DNACPR Documentation Audit on Old Age Psychiatry Wards in Aneurin Bevan University Health Board (ABUHB) in South Wales. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S272-S272. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10663.

audits.title: Escalation of care planning on an older adult inpatient unit during the COVID-19 pandemic
audits.standard: GMC recommendations on discussion of cardiopulmonary resuscitation and escalation of care
audits.setting: Older adult mental health inpatient unit, Angelton Clinic, Bridgend

cycle1.result: 18% of notes had escalation of care plans; 84% had DNAR forms.

audits.intervention: New escalation of care proforma designed with MDT input, implemented through education and communication with the medical team.

cycle2.result: 78% of notes had completed escalation of care forms; 83% had completed DNAR forms.

audits.other_findings: Unit nurse practitioner to champion completion; proformas made available on all inpatient wards.
audits.citation: McDermott A, Rankin J. Escalation of care planning on an older adult inpatient unit during the COVID-19 pandemic. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S90-S91.

audits.title: Do not attempt cardiopulmonary resuscitation documentation: a quality improvement project.
audits.standard: All Wales DNACPR policy and audit template
audits.setting: Velindre Cancer Centre, Welsh NHS trust

cycle1.result: Forms showed consistency in completion (figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Trust adopted the new national DNACPR form; education events on the all Wales policy; TalkCPR videos and e-learning modules disseminated.

cycle2.result: Clearer documentation of discussions with patients and families, and of reasons why and when conversations had not taken place; improved in several domains.

audits.other_findings: Authors suggest a central electronic record for advance care plans could improve further.
audits.citation: Haire E, Bralesford C, Botting J, Beasant E, Taubert M. Do not attempt cardiopulmonary resuscitation documentation: a quality improvement project. BMJ Support Palliat Care. 2023. doi:10.1136/spcare-2022-004133. PMID: 37258086.
